nodes.label: work
nodes.why: The whole repository. Every feature below is part of it.

nodes.label: Usage Data Exploration
nodes.why: It spans selecting date ranges and analyzing bike usage data.

nodes.label: Bike Usage Analytics
nodes.why: This subsystem spans date-scoped bike data analysis, time-window selection, metrics, charts, and dashboard presentation.

nodes.label: Yearly Summary Table
nodes.why: This feature renders yearly bicycle-count summaries with totals and east-west breakdowns.

nodes.label: Event Day Labels
nodes.why: This feature defines labels for tracked abnormal days such as storms and holidays.

nodes.label: Ride Pattern Analysis
nodes.why: It presents hourly weekday and weekend averages alongside monthly, directional, and event-adjusted ride totals.

nodes.label: Date-Scoped Bike Dashboard
nodes.why: This feature provides the bicycle-count dashboard with date filtering, charting, downloads, and event-aware averages.

nodes.label: Hourly Ride Averages
nodes.why: This feature displays average bicycle rides grouped by hour of day.

nodes.label: Monthly Totals
nodes.why: This feature renders monthly bicycle-count totals and supports seasonal and by-year views.

nodes.label: Daily CSV Download
nodes.why: It provides a CSV download containing daily bicycle-count totals.

nodes.label: Date Window Selection
nodes.why: This feature parses a requested date range and defaults it to the last complete year.

nodes.label: East-West Share Trends
nodes.why: This feature compares east and west counts over time while showing their changing share.

nodes.label: East-West Comparison
nodes.why: This feature provides a page comparing bicycle counts from the east and west sides.

nodes.label: Date Window
nodes.why: It limits each page’s data to a selected date range, defaulting to the last complete year.

atoms.subject: mark tracked event days on the daily and monthly charts
atoms.prompt: on the daily and monthly charts, make the event days we track stand out from the ordinary ones, so nobody reads a spike as growth when it was a heat wave. however you think is clearest
rationale: hm no, not a shaded band behind the whole day
make the event days we track stand out from the ordinary ones

atoms.subject: add a by-hour page showing average rides per hour
atoms.prompt: so the committee paper needs a chart of what time of day people actually ride, which i cant get out of the csv by hand. can you add a page showing the average count for each hour of the day, and call out the busiest hour at the top so nobody has to read the chart to get the headline. link it from the nav as well
rationale: add a page showing the average count for each hour of the day

atoms.subject: scope every page to a picked date window, default last complete year
atoms.prompt: right, bigger job, and im not sure how much work it is. the dashboard always shows the whole file which is seven years now, so the seasonal chart is a hairball and two people looking at two pages are looking at different periods without knowing it. let me pick a start and end date and have every page respect it. default to the last complete year, not the last 365 days, because when the paper says 2024 it has to mean 2024. the picker can be as dumb as two text boxes, i genuinely dont care what it looks like, but everything has to respect it including the csv download, otherwise someone downloads the csv, gets different numbers to the page they were just looking at, and i have to explain that in a meeting
rationale: pick a start and end date and have every page respect it

atoms.subject: track known non-normal days like storms and holidays
atoms.prompt: there are days in here that are nothing like a normal day. the february 2019 snowstorm, christmas, the fourth of july, that sort of thing. start keeping track of which days those are so we can tell them apart later. theres a list in my email i will paste in later, for now put in the handful you can find by looking at the numbers and leave it easy to add more
rationale: start keeping track of which days those are so we can tell them apart…

atoms.subject: round bike counts on the overview page to the nearest 10
atoms.prompt: the numbers on the front page are quoted down to the single bike and thats false precision for a sensor like this. round them sensibly wherever we show them
rationale: round them sensibly wherever we show them

atoms.subject: ugh revert f-0289065103b82135f1b13615f026fa3d44ab55b7099de26f83d3defd6c43c11f@1
add a monthly totals page to see the seasonal swing
atoms.prompt: add a page showing the total for each month back to the start of the file, as a chart. the point of it is to see the summer dip when the weather turns. put the highest and lowest month in words above the chart
rationale: add a page showing the total for each month back to the start of the…

atoms.subject: add a csv download link for daily totals
atoms.prompt: we shoudl proably have a csv download somewhere. the reason is people keep asking me to email them the daily numbers and i export it by hand out of the notebook every time, which takes ten minutes and i get it wrong about a third of the time. add a download link that gives back the daily totals as a csv so i can stop doing it by hand
rationale: add a download link that gives back the daily totals as a csv so i can…

atoms.subject: split the by-hour page into weekday and weekend charts
atoms.prompt: commuters and weekend riders are two different crowds and the paper treats them seperately, so the single line we have now describes neither of them. split the hour of day page so weekdays and weekends can be seen side by side. keep the combined view as well though, i still want it
rationale: split the hour of day page so weekdays and weekends can be seen side…

atoms.subject: exclude event days from averages, keep them in totals
atoms.prompt: ok this is the one thats been bugging me for weeks. the averages are being pulled around by the event days -- a snowbound monday is not what an average sunday looks like, and the quiet-day figure we quoted in the report is basically wrong because of it. keep them out of the averages wherever we show one, but do not lose them from the totals or the daily table, the totals are what the funding number is built on and dropping a real ride out of a total would be misreporting. and it has to be the same rule on every page, i dont want the monthly page doing one thing and the by-year table doing another
rationale: keep them out of the averages wherever we show one

atoms.subject: add an east vs west comparison page
atoms.prompt: theres a sensor on each side of the bridge and people keep asking me whether the two sides are balanced, which i cant answer. add a page comparing east and west: totals for each, and how the split changes across the hours of the day
rationale: add a page comparing east and west

atoms.subject: show the east/west split drifting over time, keep totals summed
atoms.prompt: someone said one of the two sensors reads low and has done for a while. have a look at the two series yourself, decide whether we should still be adding them together for the headline numbers, and do whatever you conclude is right. put your reasoning in the message so i can point at it when somebody files a fault report
rationale: decide whether we should still be adding them together for the…

"""Whether the east and west sidewalks carry the same traffic, and when they don't.""" from bikecount import charts, metrics from bikecount.pages import shell PATH = "/sides" TITLE = "East vs West" ORDER = 3 def render(readings, start, end): east, west = metrics.side_totals(readings) total = east + west share_by_hour = metrics.hourly_west_share(readings) share_by_year = metrics.west_share_by_year(readings) by_hour = lambda h: f"{h:02d}:00" rows = "".join(f"{h:02d}:00{s}% west" for h, s in share_by_hour) return shell("East vs West", f"""

East sidewalk

{east:,}

{round(100 * east / total)}% of all riders

West sidewalk

{west:,}

{round(100 * west / total)}% of all riders

West sidewalk's share of riders, by hour of day

{charts.bar_chart(share_by_hour, label=by_hour)}

A bar at 50% means the two sides split evenly that hour.

{rows}
HourSplit

West sidewalk's share of riders, by year

{charts.bar_chart(share_by_year)}

West's share held at 48-49% from the start of the file through 2015, then began climbing every year after and hasn't levelled off. That is not what a change in riders' habits looks like — it looks like the east sensor reading low, and getting worse. We still add the two sides together for the totals elsewhere on this dashboard, since they count different sidewalks rather than the same one twice, but a year-on-year total comparison that spans 2016 is comparing a good count against a drifting one.

""", start, end)

"""One row per year: total, average day and busiest day. The table for the front of the quarterly report.""" from bikecount import metrics from bikecount.pages import shell PATH = "/years" TITLE = "By Year" ORDER = 4 def render(readings, start, end): years = metrics.yearly_summary(readings) rows = "".join( f"{year}{total:,}{avg:,}{count:,}{day:%d %b}" for year, total, avg, day, count in years ) partial_years = [] if (start.month, start.day) != (1, 1): partial_years.append(years[0][0]) if (end.month, end.day) != (12, 31): partial_years.append(years[-1][0]) partial_years = list(dict.fromkeys(partial_years)) caveat = "" if partial_years: names = " and ".join(str(y) for y in partial_years) noun = "a partial year" if len(partial_years) == 1 else "partial years" verb = "is" if len(partial_years) == 1 else "are" caveat = f'

{names} {verb} {noun} in this window — it runs {start:%d %b %Y} to {end:%d %b %Y}.

' return shell("By Year", f"""

One row per year, {start:%d %b %Y} to {end:%d %b %Y}

{rows}
YearTotalAverage dayBusiest dayDate
{caveat}

Total is east + west sidewalks added together. The east sensor looks to be reading low and getting worse since around 2016 (see East vs West), so treat a total for 2016 onward as a bigger undercount than a total from before it — the two aren't a clean before/after comparison.

""", start, end)

atoms.subject: mark tracked event days on the daily and monthly charts
atoms.prompt: on the daily and monthly charts, make the event days we track stand out from the ordinary ones, so nobody reads a spike as growth when it was a heat wave. however you think is clearest
rationale: hm no, not a shaded band behind the whole day
make the event days we track stand out from the ordinary ones

atoms.subject: add a by-hour page showing average rides per hour
atoms.prompt: so the committee paper needs a chart of what time of day people actually ride, which i cant get out of the csv by hand. can you add a page showing the average count for each hour of the day, and call out the busiest hour at the top so nobody has to read the chart to get the headline. link it from the nav as well
rationale: add a page showing the average count for each hour of the day

atoms.subject: scope every page to a picked date window, default last complete year
atoms.prompt: right, bigger job, and im not sure how much work it is. the dashboard always shows the whole file which is seven years now, so the seasonal chart is a hairball and two people looking at two pages are looking at different periods without knowing it. let me pick a start and end date and have every page respect it. default to the last complete year, not the last 365 days, because when the paper says 2024 it has to mean 2024. the picker can be as dumb as two text boxes, i genuinely dont care what it looks like, but everything has to respect it including the csv download, otherwise someone downloads the csv, gets different numbers to the page they were just looking at, and i have to explain that in a meeting
rationale: pick a start and end date and have every page respect it

atoms.subject: track known non-normal days like storms and holidays
atoms.prompt: there are days in here that are nothing like a normal day. the february 2019 snowstorm, christmas, the fourth of july, that sort of thing. start keeping track of which days those are so we can tell them apart later. theres a list in my email i will paste in later, for now put in the handful you can find by looking at the numbers and leave it easy to add more
rationale: start keeping track of which days those are so we can tell them apart…

atoms.subject: round bike counts on the overview page to the nearest 10
atoms.prompt: the numbers on the front page are quoted down to the single bike and thats false precision for a sensor like this. round them sensibly wherever we show them
rationale: round them sensibly wherever we show them

atoms.prompt: add a page showing the total for each month back to the start of the file, as a chart. the point of it is to see the summer dip when the weather turns. put the highest and lowest month in words above the chart
rationale: add a page showing the total for each month back to the start of the…

atoms.subject: add a csv download link for daily totals
atoms.prompt: we shoudl proably have a csv download somewhere. the reason is people keep asking me to email them the daily numbers and i export it by hand out of the notebook every time, which takes ten minutes and i get it wrong about a third of the time. add a download link that gives back the daily totals as a csv so i can stop doing it by hand
rationale: add a download link that gives back the daily totals as a csv so i can…

atoms.subject: split the by-hour page into weekday and weekend charts
atoms.prompt: commuters and weekend riders are two different crowds and the paper treats them seperately, so the single line we have now describes neither of them. split the hour of day page so weekdays and weekends can be seen side by side. keep the combined view as well though, i still want it
rationale: split the hour of day page so weekdays and weekends can be seen side…

atoms.subject: exclude event days from averages, keep them in totals
atoms.prompt: ok this is the one thats been bugging me for weeks. the averages are being pulled around by the event days -- a snowbound monday is not what an average sunday looks like, and the quiet-day figure we quoted in the report is basically wrong because of it. keep them out of the averages wherever we show one, but do not lose them from the totals or the daily table, the totals are what the funding number is built on and dropping a real ride out of a total would be misreporting. and it has to be the same rule on every page, i dont want the monthly page doing one thing and the by-year table doing another
rationale: keep them out of the averages wherever we show one

atoms.subject: add an east vs west comparison page
atoms.prompt: theres a sensor on each side of the bridge and people keep asking me whether the two sides are balanced, which i cant answer. add a page comparing east and west: totals for each, and how the split changes across the hours of the day
rationale: add a page comparing east and west

atoms.subject: show the east/west split drifting over time, keep totals summed
atoms.prompt: someone said one of the two sensors reads low and has done for a while. have a look at the two series yourself, decide whether we should still be adding them together for the headline numbers, and do whatever you conclude is right. put your reasoning in the message so i can point at it when somebody files a fault report
rationale: decide whether we should still be adding them together for the…

"""What time of day people ride: the average count for each hour.""" from bikecount import charts, metrics from bikecount.pages import shell PATH = "/hourly" TITLE = "By Hour" ORDER = 1 def render(readings, start, end): hours = metrics.hourly_averages(readings) hour, avg = max(hours, key=lambda kv: kv[1]) rows = "".join(f"{h:02d}:00{a:,}" for h, a in hours) weekday = metrics.hourly_averages_weekday(readings) weekend = metrics.hourly_averages_weekend(readings) by_hour = lambda h: f"{h:02d}:00" return shell("By Hour", f"""

Busiest hour of day

{hour:02d}:00

average {avg:,} bikes an hour

Average count by hour of day

{charts.bar_chart(hours, label=by_hour)} {rows}
HourAvg bikes

Weekday vs weekend

Weekday

{charts.bar_chart(weekday, label=by_hour)}

Weekend

{charts.bar_chart(weekend, label=by_hour)}
""", start, end)
